meta.titre: Kitchen Safety and Accident Prevention: Planning the Kitchen and Preventing Burns, Falls, Cuts and Fires
meta.sous_theme: Well-planned kitchen, causes of kitchen accidents and prevention rules

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: The kitchen is where many home accidents happen: a child pulls a pot handle, a spill on the floor makes someone slip, or cooking oil catches fire. Most of these accidents can be avoided by planning the kitchen well and following simple safety rules. This is why the GCE asks you to give a stated number of rules to prevent burns, falls, cuts or fires, and to say what makes a kitchen well planned. A mark is gained for each rule, so learn them as clear short sentences.

items: A burn is caused by dry heat and a scald by hot liquid or steam.
Water conducts electricity, so wet hands and electricity are dangerous.
Oil is lighter than water and burns easily when it is too hot.

sections.titre: A safe kitchen: planning and prevention rules
sections.contenu_markdown:
### A well-planned kitchen
A well-planned kitchen is safe, efficient and pleasant to work in. Its main features are:
- the cooker, sink and refrigerator arranged to form a **work triangle**, so that movement between them is short and easy;
- enough **work surfaces** and **storage**, with heavy items stored low;
- good **lighting** and **ventilation**, so that smoke, steam and gas escape;
- a **non-slip, washable floor** and surfaces that are easy to clean;
- sockets and appliances placed safely, away from water.

### Preventing accidents
| Accident | Rules |
|---|---|
| Burns and scalds | Turn pot handles inwards and away from the edge; use dry oven gloves, not a wet cloth; keep children away from the cooker; lift lids away from your face; do not overfill pans; do not wear loose, hanging clothes near a flame. |
| Falls | Wipe up spills at once; keep the floor clear and dry; use non-slip mats and sturdy steps, not a chair; store things within reach; keep the kitchen well lit. |
| Cuts | Keep knives sharp and use the right knife on a board; cut away from the body; store knives in a block; never put a knife in washing-up water; sweep up broken glass with care. |
| Electric shock | Switch off before cleaning; dry hands; repair damaged flex; do not overload sockets; keep appliances away from water. |
| Fire and gas | Never leave hot oil alone; smother an oil fire with a lid or fire blanket, never water; keep cloths and paper away from the flame; for a gas leak close the cylinder valve and open windows. |
| Poisoning | Keep cleaning products labelled, in their own containers, away from food and children. |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to state or enumerate a number of rules or measures.
variantes.contenu_markdown: One rule is one mark (or two if the question gives 10 marks for 5 rules). Write each rule as a short instruction beginning with a verb: "Turn the pot handles inwards." Add a few words of reason only if the question says "explain" or if marks are clearly 2 per point. Give the exact number asked; extra rules do not earn extra marks, and one wrong rule among them may lose a mark.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked what to do in an emergency.
variantes.contenu_markdown: For an oil or fat fire, switch off the heat if it is safe, and cover the pan with a lid or a fire blanket to cut off air. Never pour water on it and never carry the burning pan. For an electrical fire switch off the power if you can reach the switch safely. If the fire spreads, leave the room, close the door and call for help.

sections.enonce_markdown: Enumerate four rules that a household should follow when frying food in hot oil. (8 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "Enumerate" means list, and 8 marks for four rules means 2 marks for each, so each rule needs a short reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Four rules, each with a short reason.

etapes.action: Think of the dangers of hot oil.
etapes.justification: Hot oil can splash and burn the skin, catch fire if overheated, and be knocked over.
Different rules for different dangers earn separate marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Handle position, supervision, dry food, a lid nearby.

etapes.action: Write each rule with its reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Turn the pan handle inwards so that it cannot be knocked or pulled. 2. Never leave the pan unattended because oil can overheat and catch fire. 3. Dry wet food before putting it in, because water makes the hot oil spit and burn. 4. Keep a lid or fire blanket near to smother a fire, and never use water on it.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Turn pan handles inwards, never leave hot oil alone, dry food before frying, and keep a lid or fire blanket ready to smother any fire.

items.erreur_markdown: Pouring water on a pan of burning oil.
items.pourquoi_faux: Water sinks under the oil and turns to steam, which throws burning oil about and spreads the fire.
items.correction_markdown: Smother the flames with a lid or a fire blanket after switching off the heat.

items.erreur_markdown: Picking up a hot pot with a wet cloth.
items.pourquoi_faux: Water conducts heat quickly, so the heat reaches your hand and causes a scald or burn.
items.correction_markdown: Use dry oven gloves or a thick dry cloth.

items.erreur_markdown: Standing on a chair to reach a high shelf.
items.pourquoi_faux: A chair can slip or tip, and falls are a common accident.
items.correction_markdown: Use a sturdy step ladder and store the things in daily use within easy reach.

items.erreur_markdown: Leaving a knife in the washing-up bowl.
items.pourquoi_faux: It cannot be seen in the water and cuts the person who puts a hand in.
items.correction_markdown: Wash knives separately, dry them and put them in a knife block.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Name the three appliances that form the work triangle in a well-planned kitchen. (b) State two features of a safe kitchen floor. (c) State one rule that prevents a child from pulling a hot pot off the cooker.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Cooker, sink and refrigerator**. (b) Any two of **non-slip, washable, dry, free of clutter**. (c) Turn the pot handles inwards, away from the edge, or keep children away from the cooker.

items.enonce_markdown: A family wants to make its kitchen safer and buys 2 non-slip mats at $2\,500$ FCFA each, 1 pair of oven gloves at $1\,500$ FCFA, 1 knife block at $6\,000$ FCFA and 1 fire blanket at $8\,000$ FCFA (assumed prices). (a) Find the total cost. (b) The family has $25\,000$ FCFA. How much is left? (c) Say which accident each item helps to prevent.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Mats: $2 \times 2\,500 = 5\,000$. Gloves: $1\,500$. Knife block: $6\,000$. Fire blanket: $8\,000$. Total: $5\,000 + 1\,500 + 6\,000 + 8\,000 = 20\,500$, so **$20\,500$ FCFA**. (b) $25\,000 - 20\,500 = 4\,500$, so **$4\,500$ FCFA** is left. (c) Mats: falls. Oven gloves: burns and scalds. Knife block: cuts. Fire blanket: fires (it smothers the flames).

items.enonce_markdown: Describe the hazards in this kitchen and say how each should be dealt with. A pan handle sticks out over the edge of the cooker. Water has been spilled near the sink. A kettle has a frayed flex. A knife lies in the washing-up bowl. A pan of hot oil has been left on the cooker while the cook goes to answer a call, and a curtain hangs near the cooker. Give your answer in the form of five hazards, each with one action.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each hazard with a matching action: (1) **Handle over the edge**: it can be knocked or pulled by a child, so turn it inwards. (2) **Spilled water**: someone may slip, so wipe it at once and use a non-slip mat. (3) **Frayed flex**: there is a risk of electric shock or fire, so unplug it and have the flex repaired or replaced. (4) **Knife in the bowl**: it may cut a hand, so wash it separately, dry it and put it in a knife block. (5) **Oil left unattended and a curtain near the cooker**: the oil may overheat and catch fire, so switch off the heat when leaving, never leave hot oil alone and move or tie back the curtain.

items_markdown: A well-planned kitchen has a work triangle (cooker, sink, refrigerator), enough work surfaces and storage, good light and ventilation, and a safe non-slip floor.
Burns: handles inwards, dry gloves, children away from the cooker, lids lifted away from the face.
Falls: wipe spills at once, keep floors clear, use non-slip mats and a sturdy step. Cuts: sharp knife on a board, cut away from the body, store in a block.
Fire: never leave hot oil alone, smother with a lid or fire blanket, never use water on an oil fire; for a gas leak close the cylinder valve and open windows.
Electricity: dry hands, switch off before cleaning, repair frayed flex, do not overload sockets.
For "state five rules" write exactly five short instructions, each starting with a verb.
